Incorporating Beige Book insights into the SLOOS-adjusted read of the March 15, 2020 FOMC statement:

- Beige Book anecdotes point to mixed but deteriorating conditions as COVID-19 risks rose: travel and tourism weakened notably, manufacturers reported emerging supply-chain disruptions, natural resource extraction/energy declined, and loan growth was being impacted. At the same time, some areas showed resilience (certain nonfinancial services, transportation pockets like Mid-Atlantic ports, and largely little-changed agricultural conditions), and labor markets were still tight heading into the shock.
- These district reports corroborate the FOMC’s acknowledgement of stress in energy and rising downside risks, and they align with SLOOS signals of tighter bank standards and reduced risk tolerance that will dampen credit transmission in the near term.
- However, because Beige Book conditions were not yet uniformly weak across sectors or regions at that time, they modestly temper the SLOOS-only negativity by highlighting ongoing activity in select services and transportation and a still-solid starting point for labor markets.

Net: The balance of risks remains negative given tightening bank credit and sharp downturns in travel/energy, but Beige Book evidence of partial resilience softens the immediate drag versus a SLOOS-only lens.
